messages:
maya_ops: Heads-up — product asked for a Q4 capacity plan for the new chat feature. Need throughput & GPU-hour projection for holiday peak (assume 2x baseline). Can folks sanity-check numbers and call out headroom we should reserve?

ben_infra: Quick baseline metrics I pulled from last month for rw-7B-q4 (A100 class): ~2,500 tokens/sec per GPU under typical request mix (avg req out = 75 tokens, in = 25 -> 100 tokens/req). GPU util target today ~65%.

maya_ops: Ok — assume avg request = 100 tokens. If peak QPS = 200, tokens/sec required = 20k t/s.

ben_infra: Right. Calculation:```
# tokens/sec needed = QPS * avg_tokens_per_req
tokens_per_req = 100
peak_qps = 200
tokens_sec_needed = peak_qps * tokens_per_req  # 20_000 t/s
gpus_needed_nominal = ceil(tokens_sec_needed / 2500)  # 8 GPUs
```

ben_infra: If we want 30% headroom for burstiness & model variance: GPUs = ceil(8 * 1.3) = 11. So plan for 11 GPUs at peak.

carla_sre: I recommend we target 60% utilization ceiling for autoscaler (i.e., scale up before GPUs hit 80% sustained). That gives us latency headroom. If we plan for 11 GPUs at 65% we'd be at ~45% util with provisioned headroom — sounds ok.

maya_ops: Translate to GPU-hours: 11 GPUs * 24h = 264 GPU-hours/day -> monthly (30d) = 7,920 GPU-hours.

ben_infra: Cost estimate (rough): assume $4/GPU-hour for reserved Dedicated fleet -> monthly = 7,920 * $4 = $31,680. If we use shared hosted capacity with spot-like pricing we might get average $2.5/hr but risk preemption / throttles.

sam_product: Q: how much does avg request length variance affect this? If avg tokens jumps to 150, how many GPUs then?

ben_infra: If avg tokens = 150: tokens_sec_needed = 200 * 150 = 30k t/s -> nominal GPUs = ceil(30_000/2500)=12 -> with 30% headroom -> 16 GPUs. GPU-hours/day=384. Monthly cost @ $4=384*30*4=$46,080.

carla_sre: Also account for cold-start and KV cache warm-up. If requests use long prefixes (context reuse), effective tokens/sec per GPU can improve because of prefix caching; conversely many short independent requests reduce batching efficiency and lower tokens/sec. We should instrument: metric 'tokens_emitted/sec_by_model' + 'gpu_util_by_gpu' + 'prefix_cache_hit_rate'.

raja_capacitybot: Forecast snapshot (auto):
- baseline_qps: 100
- expected_peak_qps: 200 (2x)
- baseline_avg_tokens: 100
- per_gpu_tps: 2500 t/s
- peak_gpus_no_headroom: 8
- peak_gpus_with_30pct_headroom: 11
- peak_gpu_hours_day: 264
- est_monthly_gpu_hours_30d: 7920
- est_monthly_cost_reserved @$4h: $31,680
Link to detailed spreadsheet: https://redwood.internal/s/forecast/q4-chat (internal)

maya_ops: Notes on operational mitigations: pre-warm a small burst pool (2-3 GPUs) in region, enable cross-region fallback to us-east if us-west saturates, and add an autoscale policy with 90s cooldown and scale-step of +2 GPUs. Also add a canary rollout for new model variant to avoid sudden perf regressions.

ben_infra: Region constraints: current Dedicated capacity in eu-west is limited (we have 6 spare GPUs). If customer demand shifts EU-heavy we'll need to shift some reserved capacity or enable routing to hosted with throttling.

sam_product: Performance SLAs to product: target p95 latency < 450ms for short requests (<64 tokens) and < 1.2s for typical generation. Do we meet that at 65% util?

carla_sre: Yes for short requests if batching latency is controlled. We should target steady-state GPU util ~60-70%. If we hit sustained >75% p95 will increase; rely on autoscaler rules.

maya_ops: Action items: 1) ben -> finalize spreadsheet with scenarios (avg tokens 80/100/150), cost lines for reserved vs hosted. 2) carla -> add monitoring dashboards for tokens/sec_by_model, prefix_cache_hit_rate, per-gpu util; set alert at 75% per-gpu sustained. 3) infra -> pre-warm plan: +3 GPUs in us-west at T-2 days for major sale days. 4) product -> confirm acceptable cost vs latency tradeoff.

ben_infra: I'll drop the spreadsheet link here by EOD and tag you all.

maya_ops: Thanks — this is enough to brief finance and ops. :thumbsup:
